import re
import sys
from contextlib import suppress
from typing import Iterable, NamedTuple, Optional

from .color import Color
from .style import Style
from .text import Text

re_ansi = re.compile(
    r"""
(?:\x1b\](.*?)\x1b\\)|
(?:\x1b([(@-Z\\-_]|\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]))
""",
    re.VERBOSE,
)


class _AnsiToken(NamedTuple):
    """Result of ansi tokenized string."""

    plain: str = ""
    sgr: Optional[str] = ""
    osc: Optional[str] = ""


def _ansi_tokenize(ansi_text: str) -> Iterable[_AnsiToken]:
    """Tokenize a string in to plain text and ANSI codes.

    Args:
        ansi_text (str): A String containing ANSI codes.

    Yields:
        AnsiToken: A named tuple of (plain, sgr, osc)
    """

    position = 0
    sgr: Optional[str]
    osc: Optional[str]
    for match in re_ansi.finditer(ansi_text):
        start, end = match.span(0)
        osc, sgr = match.groups()
        if start > position:
            yield _AnsiToken(ansi_text[position:start])
        if sgr:
            if sgr == "(":
                position = end + 1
                continue
            if sgr.endswith("m"):
                yield _AnsiToken("", sgr[1:-1], osc)
        else:
            yield _AnsiToken("", sgr, osc)
        position = end
    if position < len(ansi_text):
        yield _AnsiToken(ansi_text[position:])

from rich.ansi import _ansi_tokenize, _AnsiToken

def test_ansi_tokenize():
    test_cases = [
        ("Hello\x1b7World", "HelloWorld"),
        ("Hello\x1b8World", "HelloWorld"),
        ("Hello\x1b0World", "HelloWorld"),
        ("Hello\x1b?World", "HelloWorld"),
        ("Hello\x1b@World", "HelloWorld"),
        ("Hello\x1b[mWorld", "HelloWorld"), # This is an SGR, but it is handled differently
    ]
    
    for input_text, expected_plain in test_cases:
        tokens = list(_ansi_tokenize(input_text))
        plain = "".join(t.plain for t in tokens)
        print(f"Input: {repr(input_text)}, Plain: {repr(plain)}, Expected: {repr(expected_plain)}, Match: {plain == expected_plain}")

test_ansi_tokenize()
